\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Risk cases parseable under both conditions ($n$). Out: trap failure under the first condition only ($b$); in: under the second condition only ($c$). Difference $=(c-b)/n$, the second condition's trap-failure rate minus the first's, in percentage points, with the Newcombe method-10 95\% CI for paired proportions \citep{newcombe1998improved}; $p$: exact two-sided McNemar test \citep{mcnemar1947note}. When $c=0$ the exact test reduces to a sign test on the $b$ discordant pairs, $p=2\cdot0.5^{b}$, a function of $b$ alone. C2$\to$C4 adds no failure ($c=0$) mainly by design: repair adds no text to the supported side and never upgrades a requirement status; the other paths that could add one (subjective-family downgrade, requirement deduplication, regeneration) added none in these data. qwen3:30b-a3b has no discordant C0$\to$C5 pair (0/72), so no interval is reported. Intervals and tests are pointwise, without multiplicity adjustment. C1 and C2 differ in wording, fields, the validator header sentence and length, so C1$\to$C2 does not isolate the representation of the rules. Clearance rows: $n$ = paired risk cases that fail under C2; k = those no longer failing under C4; Wilson 95\% CI for per-model estimates. Pooled rows repeat each case across models, so only counts and point estimates are reported, without intervals or tests.\par}
